properties.statement:
① SYMPTOM, as reported by Alex (v0.47.0, macOS, 2026-09-05): loop_status reports it cannot read /proc/self/exe so it cannot confirm whether the running server is current — 'unknown, verify another way' — on every non-Linux run. Expected: a yes/no, or at worst one notice per session. Not affected: Linux, where the same call answers stale/current.

② PRECEDENT: cap:the-server-knows-its-own-currency and chg:the-server-says-when-it-is-stale-20260809 built the check; fact:defect-a-running-server-cannot-say-it-is-stale is the defect it closed. None mention a platform. req:platform states 'Runs on Linux and macOS developer machines.'

③ CANDIDATES: (a) the check uses a Linux-only primitive with no portable fallback; (b) the unknown answer is honest and correct, and the defect is only that the note is carried on every call rather than once; (c) the report is from a build predating the check. ④ DISCRIMINATOR: read the implementation — (a) predicts a literal /proc path with no cfg branch; (b) predicts a platform-neutral check whose note is attached unconditionally; (c) predicts the note text absent from 0.47.0.

⑤ MEASURED (code, 2026-09-05): service.rs:149 exe_replaced_since_start does `std::fs::read_link("/proc/self/exe")` and on Err returns (None, UNKNOWN_NOTE); the stale verdict comes from the link ending in ' (deleted)'. No cfg(target_os) branch, no fallback. So (a) is TRUE: on macOS read_link fails every time and the answer is always unknown. AND (b) is ALSO true as the amplifier: coherence.rs:278-300 attaches served_by with stale_note, and when stale != Some(false) pushes the note into `next` — on every loop_status. (c) refuted: the check shipped 2026-08-09, well before 0.47.0. ⭐ AND THE PORTABLE PRIMITIVE ALREADY EXISTS IN THE SAME MODULE: shared.rs:115 exe_fingerprint() uses std::env::current_exe() + fs::metadata (size:mtime) and is what client election compares (cap:a-client-elects-a-server-of-its-own-build). A 'replaced since start' answer is one comparison away — fingerprint at startup vs fingerprint now.

⑥ CLASS: a Linux-only primitive used where the portable one already exists beside it, on a project whose accepted requirement names macOS. The instance is /proc/self/exe; the class is 'currency has no non-Linux answer'. Would this fix have prevented earlier reports? No earlier non-Linux report exists on the record — Alex is the only macOS user — which is why it went a month unnoticed.

FIX SHAPE: keep the (deleted)-link check as primary on Linux (it is stronger: it sees a replaced binary even with equal size and mtime), and fall back to fingerprint-at-start vs fingerprint-now everywhere. Pin with a pure function (start_fp, now_fp) -> verdict, tested failing-first. With a real answer on macOS, the per-call note disappears by construction; whether an UNKNOWN answer (both paths failing) should still be carried on every call or once per session is a smaller second question.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: not run on macOS here (Linux box) — the read_link failure on darwin is inferred from the platform (no /proc), not observed. Fingerprint equality after a replace-with-identical-size-and-mtime is a false 'current'; rare, and the Linux primary path does not have it.
properties.value: {"cause":"exe_replaced_since_start reads /proc/self/exe, no cfg branch, no fallback -> None on non-Linux","amplifier":"loop_status carries stale_note into next on every call when stale != Some(false)","portable_primitive_exists":"shared.rs exe_fingerprint (current_exe + size:mtime)","violates":"req:platform (macOS)","refuted":"old-build candidate; check shipped 2026-08-09","not_run_on":"macOS"}
